text:
Ana: Heads-up — POC with NexusOps hitting intermittent timeouts when using our TS SDK behind their corporate forward proxy. They see 504s after ~30s during streaming responses.
Sam: Can you paste the exact error and SDK version?
Ana: Error from their app: `FetchError: request to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat failed, reason: socket hang up`
Ana: Using @redwood-js v0.9.2, node 18, proxy requires CONNECT auth. We tried bumping client `timeout` to 60000 but long streams still drop. Logs show TLS handshake succeeded, then socket closed mid-stream.
Jordan: Do they have an idle TCP timeout on the proxy? Many corporate proxies drop long-lived upstream connections if there's no activity for X secs. Streaming can look idle between chunks.
Mike: For Node clients you can enable http(s) agent keep-alive. Quick snippet: `const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, timeout: 0 }); const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, agent, timeout: 120000 });`
Ana: The customer runs in AWS Lambda (node) so they don't control lower-level agent much. Lambda reuses connections but short-lived functions complicate persistent agents. Any Lambda-specific guidance?
Sam: In Lambda, you should reuse the SDK client across invocations (init outside handler) so the underlying Agent is reused. If they can't, fallback to buffered responses to avoid long-lived SSE streams.
NexusOps (customer): We can't change proxy timeouts or proxy config on our side. Is there a Redwood config we can flip to avoid these long-lived sockets?
Jordan: Two immediate options: (1) Use `response_mode: "buffered"` in the SDK so the server sends a single buffered response — no streaming connection to keep alive. (2) Use our internal `stream_keepalive_ms` which emits benign keepalive frames; not yet public but we can provide a patched client build.
Mike: Also check retry behavior: when the proxy returns 502/504 our JS SDK retries idempotent requests. For streamed calls retries are disabled to avoid duplication — ensure they aren't wrapped by a generic retry middleware.
Ana: Customer prefers not to install experimental builds. They asked for sample code for buffered mode and a note on pricing impact (buffered may increase perceived latency and token billing stays the same).
Sam: Draft snippet for buffered mode (Node):
```js
// init once outside handler
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, timeout: 120000 });
const resp = await client.chat.create({
  model: 'rwd-1.0',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'summarize ...' }],
  response_mode: 'buffered'
});
console.log(await resp.text());
```
Sam: Pricing note: buffered mode doesn't change per-token pricing; however, because calls finish only after the full response, it may increase duration-related costs for server-side timeouts. For POC we recommend increasing server request timeout to 2m.
Ana: I'll propose: (A) switch to buffered mode + raise timeouts to 2m; (B) if they want streaming, we can offer a patched SDK that sends keepalive frames (requires a dev build and dedicated API key). Which do they want?
NexusOps (customer): We'll go with (A) to keep things simple. Please send code + quick pricing blurb. We also need confirmation this won't affect role-based rate limits.
Sam: Buffered calls count as normal requests against their quota/rate limits — same per-token accounting. No special rate-limit exemption.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued — patch/stream-keepalive -> staging (ID 9876)
Ana: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll send the sample code and pricing note to NexusOps and close this POC ticket if they confirm.
Mike: FYI — I'll add a small section to the presales checklist about Lambda + corporate proxies and `response_mode` fallback.
Sam: Draft pricing blurb posted in the thread, ping me if they ask for an estimate for high-volume buffered traffic.
